value.text: {"result": {"suggestions": [{"kind": "new_thesis", "ticker": "MSFT", "statement": "The terms of Microsoft's revenue share and exclusive hosting arrangement with its model partner determine a distinct stream of partnership economics that is separate from Azure capacity growth, Copilot seat pricing and capital intensity.", "wrong_if": "Later reports show the revenue share payable to Microsoft or the exclusive hosting rights were not changed as the amendment describes, or that the partnership terms have no measurable effect on Microsoft's reported results.", "driver_ids": [], "rationale": "A first-hand reported fact states a lower revenue share percentage payable to Microsoft alongside longer exclusive hosting rights, and none of the existing pillars (Azure capacity growth, AI assistant revenue per seat, capital intensity and margin) addresses partnership contract economics.", "claim_ids": ["synthetic_000078.c1"], "sections": [{"email_id": "synthetic_000078", "quote": "The amendment reduces the percentage of the counterparty's revenue payable to Microsoft under the revenue share arrangement from 20% to 15%, effective January 1, 2027, and extends the term of Microsoft's exclusive cloud hosting rights for model training through December 31, 2029."}]}], "no_change_reason": null}}
